- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above prior peak or use 3-period moving average.
- If sentiment shows strong negative momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive low values), model underreacts; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to reflect risk-off bias.
- Model frequently overestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; apply downward bias of 3–7% for first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is high (≥0.77) and price is trending up, model often fails to capture mean reversion; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% after 10–15 days.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, check sentiment for divergence — if sentiment is weak, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence bias.
- For sentiment history with alternating highs/lows, model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of smoothing or use sentiment-weighted average for 3–5 day horizon.
